description:
Replace the counting sink from T-017 with the real rolling fMP4 segment buffer per N-005. The buffer holds the last N seconds of capture on disk, evicts old segments past the configured window, supports pinning during save, and survives helper crash for recovery in T-019.

Scope (binding):
- Implement `segment::buffer` per N-005:
  - Segment files written under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cove-screen-recorder/segments/<sessionId>/` (Linux) — chosen for tmpfs-backed performance on most distros and trivial cleanup on crash. Fall back to `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/.../segments/<sessionId>/` if `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset.
  - Each segment is a self-contained fMP4 fragment with its own `moof+mdat` and a leading `styp` per N-005 (no shared `moov` across segments — that's built at export time in T-019).
  - Segment duration target: 2 s (configurable). Each segment starts on an IDR/keyframe boundary; the encoder is requested to insert keyframes at the segment cadence (N-004 / N-005).
  - Atomic commit: write to `<segmentIndex>.mp4.partial`, fsync, rename to `<segmentIndex>.mp4`. Only renamed files are considered committed (N-005). Partial files are discarded on recovery.
- Rolling-window eviction:
  - Window length is per `replay.save` call (`durationSeconds`); the buffer keeps `max(windowSettings, longestActivePin) + 1 fragment` on disk. Eviction runs on every successful commit.
  - Disk-usage cap: configurable, default 4 GiB. If the buffer would exceed the cap, eviction is forced even if it shortens the available window; emit a `replay.segmentDiagnostics` event flagging the truncated window.
- Pinning per N-005: `replay.save` snapshots a `Vec<SegmentRef>` representing the last `durationSeconds`; the buffer increments a refcount on each `SegmentRef`. Pinned segments are NOT evicted. `replay.snapshot_release` decrements the refcount; segments with zero refcount are eligible for eviction immediately.
- Emit `replay.segmentDiagnostics` per N-007 §6 / N-005 schema, including:
  - `fragmentsReceived`, `segmentsCommitted`, `segmentsEvicted`, `segmentsPinned`, `bytesOnDisk`, `diskWriteLatencyMs`, `fsyncLatencyMs`, `renameLatencyMs`, `backPressureSustainedMs`, `partialSegmentRecovered`, `formatchangeSegments`, `bufferWindowSecondsObserved`, `bufferBytesPctOfCap`.
- Failure modes:
  - Disk full → `capture.sessionLost { reason: "segment-sink-disk-full" }` and tear down; partial segment discarded.
  - State-dir unwritable at boot → refuse `requestSession` with `segment-sink-state-dir-unwritable`.
  - Slow disk (sustained `diskWriteLatencyMs` > 250 ms) → emit `encoder.backPressure` (segment layer is the back-pressure source; encoder is the carrier) and keep going; do NOT drop frames silently.
- Recovery scaffolding (consumed by T-019):
  - On helper boot, scan `<segmentsRoot>` for any sub-directories left from a prior session. For each: discard `.partial` files; if at least one committed segment exists, register a `RecoverableSession { sessionId, segments, lastCommittedAt }` and emit `replay.recoveryAvailable` within 2 s of `engine.ready` per N-007 §6.
  - `replay.discard_recovered_session` deletes the directory. `replay.restore_recovered_session` returns a `ReplaySnapshot` over the committed segments (export wiring is T-019).
- Hook into the encoder: the `FragmentSink` from T-017 now points at this buffer.

Out of scope (binding):
- No export pipeline (T-019).
- No remux, no stream-copy, no max-compat re-encode.
- No multi-stream/multi-track support — single video track for v2.0.0.
- No audio segments.
- No SHA-256 of segment files (export-time concern).
- No tests on M2/M3/M4 — T-010c.

Acceptance criteria:
1. With T-016 + T-017 producing real frames on M1, a 60 s capture leaves a directory of ~30 committed 2-s segments plus at most one `.partial` at any instant.
2. After 60 s of continuous capture with `replay.save({durationSeconds: 30})` invoked at t=60s, the returned snapshot references the last 30 s worth of committed segments; eviction had reduced disk to ~30 s worth before the save.
3. `replay.snapshot_release` allows eviction to resume; within one segment cycle, the pinned segments are evicted.
4. Killing the helper mid-capture (SIGKILL) and relaunching produces `replay.recoveryAvailable` within 2 s of `engine.ready`, listing the committed segments from the killed session.
5. Disk full simulated via a 200 MiB tmpfs as the segments dir produces `capture.sessionLost { reason: "segment-sink-disk-full" }`; no `.partial` remains after teardown.
6. `replay.segmentDiagnostics` fires at ~1 Hz with monotonically increasing committed/evicted counters.
7. `formatchangeSegments` increments when `capture.formatChanged` fires mid-stream (a new segment starts at the format-change boundary).
8. `--simulate` mode from T-015 still works.

Verification commands:
- `cargo build -p cove-replay-engine`
- `cargo test -p cove-replay-engine`
- Manual on M1: 60 s capture; inspect segment dir; `ffprobe` a committed segment to verify it's a valid fMP4 fragment.
- Manual SIGKILL recovery: `kill -9 $(pgrep cove-replay-engine)` mid-capture, restart helper, verify recoveryAvailable event.
- Manual disk-full: setup a 200 MiB tmpfs at the segments dir, run capture, verify the sessionLost reason.
- `git status --short`

Codex review expectations:
- Confirm atomic commit uses fsync-then-rename (N-005). A bare `rename` without fsync is a regression.
- Confirm `.partial` files are NEVER referenced by `SegmentRef`.
- Confirm pinning refcounts cannot underflow.
- Confirm eviction respects pinned refcounts (zero false evictions).
- Confirm `replay.recoveryAvailable` is emitted only for sessions with at least one committed segment.
- Confirm format-change boundaries open a new segment (N-005).
- Flag any `fs::remove_dir_all` that could escape the segments root (path traversal).
- Flag any unbounded growth in in-memory segment indices for long sessions.

Failure handling:
- If sustained `diskWriteLatencyMs > 250 ms` reveals a hidden buffering issue (e.g. encoder flushing on the wrong thread), surface it through `encoder.backPressure` rather than swallowing — silent absorption of back-pressure is the v1.1.0 failure shape.

No commits, tags, or publishes from this ticket.
title: Implement rolling fMP4 segment buffer MVP
